title: RunProduct
description: One file of a run's work/ directory, read when a client asks for the view ProductOfRun. The reader opens each directory on the path and the file relative to the one before without following a link, reads the type and the link count from the open file before a byte, and reads at most `limit` bytes in the daemon's process; no program opens the file. As with RunProducts, no command creates or changes a row.

size.description: The length of the file in bytes.

text.description: The first `limit` bytes as text; absent when kind is binary.

truncated.description: True when the file holds more than `limit` bytes: `text` is its start.

limit.description: The most bytes a read answers: 1048576.

sdc.daemon.ProductKind.title: ProductKind
sdc.daemon.ProductKind.description: What a read found: text (the bytes shown are UTF-8 without a NUL byte; a partial character at a cut does not count) or binary (anything else: no text is answered).

sdc.daemon.ProductPath.title: ProductPath
sdc.daemon.ProductPath.description: The path of a file of a run, relative to the run's work/ directory (its workspace, which the cases of the run share): names joined by `/`, none of them `..` and none starting with a dot. Never absolute and never a path of the host.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.
